Seven Rounds in Rome, Zero Movement

The seventh round of Israel-Lebanon talks in Rome ended as these negotiations usually do: everyone reported progress, and nothing moved.

Beirut wanted to expand the pilot-zone model to Bint Jbeil or Khiam. Israel said no. The real dispute was not over maps but trust: who verifies that the Lebanese Army has cleared Hezbollah’s armed presence from an area? Israel wants a mechanism it can trust. 

Lebanon does not want Israel acting as the inspector of Lebanese sovereignty. That is not a technical disagreement. That is the entire war in one procedural question.

The framework is deceptively simple. Israel withdraws gradually. The Lebanese Army deploys. Hezbollah’s infrastructure is dismantled. A third party verifies it. 

But every verb has its own veto. Beirut wants the withdrawal to prove the state can return. Israel wants proof first, because it assumes Hezbollah will return the moment its troops leave.

France was floated for a possible multinational force to replace UNIFIL. Israel objected. 

Washington is considering how to strengthen the Lebanese Army — the same army Israel is being asked to trust with clearing territory it doubts can ever be truly cleared.

Meanwhile, the negotiations proceeded in Rome while artillery and airstrikes hit southern Lebanon. UNIFIL recorded 113 Israeli artillery rounds in a single day, its highest tally since late June. Diplomacy held meetings; the border held explosions.

Israel also raised the murder and disappearance of members of Lebanon’s Jewish community, demanding information on burial sites. 

Lebanon raised prisoners. The delegations discovered, once again, that history is not a file that can be moved to the bottom of the agenda.

A Lebanese diplomatic source says there may be no new round next month. Perhaps after the summer.

The villages in southern Lebanon have not been offered a summer recess.

📣 Brazil stablecoins face IMF scrutiny as crypto flows outpace capital 

🌐 IMF has called for closer oversight of Brazil’s stablecoin market as cross-border crypto flows outpace traditional capital movements. The report says cross-border crypto transactions have increased faster than conventional capital flows and now require closer regulatory attention because of their growing links with the country’s financial system. The assessment says stablecoin purchases respond much more strongly to global financial shocks than traditional portfolio investment or foreign direct investment. 

🔔 Based on the IMF’s analysis, purchases of dollar-backed stablecoins are two to three times more sensitive to external market events, raising concerns over how quickly international volatility could spread through crypto markets. Brazil has emerged as one of the world’s more active crypto markets, with stablecoins accounting for a significant share of digital asset activity. The IMF said the country’s crypto ecosystem has become increasingly connected with the traditional financial sector, making regulatory oversight more important as adoption continues to rise.

⚠️ The report acknowledges that Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has already introduced measures to regulate crypto asset service providers. Even so, the IMF said several areas still need stronger rules, including customer asset protection, stablecoin issuance requirements, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) standards.

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has conveyed his congratulations to the new heads of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy and the Basij Organization.

In a message posted on the official website of the Parliament on Tuesday morning, Ghalibaf hailed Rear Admiral Ali Ozamaei's appointment as the IRGC Navy commander, and wished him great success in the new position.
​
He said Ozamaei's effective presence in maritime defense for years and his close familiarity with the conditions, especially in the face of the recent US-Israeli-imposed war, will be helpful in commanding a Navy that is at the forefront of protecting maritime borders, national interests in the Strait of Hormuz, and the security of the Persian Gulf.
​
Stating that the IRGC Navy performed brilliantly, relying on the initiative, courage, and capability of its forces during the late founder of the Islamic Republic, Imam Khomeini and the martyred Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, the top parliamentarian said the strategic capacities of this force will flourish even more than before through the guidance of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.
​
In a separate message, Ghalibaf greeted Hojjat al-Islam Hossein Taeb for his appointment as head of the Basij Organization, saying his tenure will witness a new chapter of transformation in the volunteer forces, with people-oriented development and utilization of the country's enormous human capital.
​
According to him, the Basij needs a comprehensive and forward-looking perspective, more than ever, and the worthy appointment of Taeb by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution to head the Basij Organization for the Underprivileged would help realize one of the enduring ideals of Imam Khomeini, that is, the formation of a twenty-million-strong volunteer force.
​
Undoubtedly, Ghalibaf continued, the background and experience of the new Basij chief, as well as his precise knowledge in various fields, would create fertile ground for organizing and giving the volunteer force a platform, under the guidance of Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.

⚡️ Araghchi congratulates senior military officials on appointments by Leader

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has congratulated senior officials on their appointment to key military posts by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.

“I sincerely congratulate each and every one of you, dear brothers, on the trust placed in you by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution and on being entrusted with such important and weighty responsibilities,” the foreign minister said in a message late Monday.
​
He said the Leader’s trust in the newly appointed military officials is the result of their years-long “struggle, experience, and valuable service in defense of the Islamic Republic of Iran and in safeguarding the country’s security, independence, and territorial integrity.”
​
Araghchi added that clear manifestations of their experience and capabilities in defending Iran were seen during the two wars imposed by the United States and Israel against the country in 2025 and 2026.
​
He wished the military officials continued success in safeguarding Iran’s security, dignity, and strength in accordance with the guidance and wisdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution.
​
On Monday, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Khamenei issued separate decrees appointing six senior commanders and officials to key positions within the Armed Forces General Staff, the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), and the Basij Organization.
